findings.description: F006 validates durable_checkout only as a boolean and F002 copies it from evidence, but once the reconstructed canonical path is confirmed non-temp, C3 implies durable_checkout must be true. The plan rejects durable_checkout=true for a temp canonical path, but does not reject or recompute durable_checkout=false for a confirmed durable canonical, which could stamp records that F003 later skips.
findings.recommendation: Pin backfill confirmation to require durable_checkout === true for any confirmed non-temp canonical path, or recompute it as true instead of copying evidence; add a false-on-non-temp evidence test.

findings.description: F004 says discover --json emits scrubbed display, keys, counts, recency, suggestion status, and suggested_name, but neither F003 nor F004 pins the exact JSON field names, value types, or suggestion_status enum. That leaves the completion test and downstream metadata substrate open to incompatible interpretations.
findings.recommendation: Define the exact top-level arrays and per-row JSON schemas, including observed_count, last_seen/recency representation, path_display, canonical_repo_key, fallback registry fields, suggested_name placement, and suggestion_status enum values.

findings.description: F002 says the backfill engine holds the live writer ledger lock, while F005 says the entrypoint acquires the same lock across the F002 sequence. Without a single pinned lock owner or reentrant transaction API, implementation can double-acquire a non-reentrant lock or accidentally run part of validation outside the critical section.
findings.recommendation: Pin the lock boundary explicitly: either F005 owns the lock and calls an unlocked F002 transaction body, or F002 owns the full locked write-mode transaction and F005 only dispatches it.
